https://www.dw.com/en/famed-climber-nirm.text: Skip to content Skip to main menu Skip to more DW sites https://p.dw.com/p/5I3dq One of the climbers killed is Nepal-born Nirmal Purja, who climbed the world's 14 highest peaks in under seven months (file photo) Image: Subash Shrestha/Pacific Press/IMAGO Advertisement Celebrated climber Nirmal Purja and nine other mountaineers have been confirmed dead after an avalanche on Pakistan 's Broad Peak, his expedition company said on Saturday. The confirmation came a day after rescuers located four bodies while searching for the 10-member expedition. How did Purja and the other mountaineers die? "It is with profound sadness and immense heartbreak that we confirm that Nirmal Purja tragically lost his life following the avalanche on Broad Peak," Purja's company Elite Expeditions said in a social media post. "We have also received confirmation that other members of the expedition sadly did not survive." The climbers had been missing since Thursday, when an avalanche struck the expedition at around 6,600 meters (21,650 feet) on Broad Peak. The party is believed to have been swept away. Two Pakistan Army Aviation helicopters joined the operation on Friday, while an experienced ground team was deployed to the area where the group was last believed to have been. Pakistani security sources said four bodies had been located that day, although they had not yet been recovered. The mountain is the 12th highest in the world and lies near Pakistan's border with China (file photo) Image: Photoshot/picture alliance At the time, rescuers were still searching for the remaining members of the group. The deaths of all 10 climbers were confirmed on Saturday. The expedition included Purja and five other Nepalese climbers, including several Sherpa guides, as well as mountaineers from four other countries. They were Pakistani mountaineer Sohail Sakhi, Omani climber Nathira Ahmed, US climber Mallory Geis and China's Wang Zhong. Who was Nirmal Purja? Nirmal Purja, widely known as Nims Dai, was a British-Nepali mountaineer who became one of the best-known high-altitude climbers of his generation. The 43-year-old served with Britain's Brigade of Gurkhas and later the elite Special Boat Service before leaving the military to become a full-time mountaineer and guide. Purja shot to international fame in 2019 when he climbed all 14 of the world's mountains above 8,000 meters in just over six months, dramatically beating the previous record of nearly eight years. His feat was chronicled in the 2021 Netflix documentary "14 Peaks: Nothing Is Impossible," which helped bring him a global following. In 2021, Purja was also part of the 10-member Nepali team that completed the first winter ascent of K2, the world's second-highest mountain. Before the latest ascent, Purja had posted his hopes for the expedition on X, asking the mountain for safe passage. What is Broad Peak? Broad Peak stands at just over 8,000 meters in Pakistan's Karakoram range, close to the border with China. It is the world's 12th-highest mountain and lies only a few kilometers from the better-known K2 . Originally designated K3 during the surveying of the Karakoram, its more modern name refers to its unusually wide summit ridge, which stretches for roughly 1.5 kilometers (just under a mile). The region contains five of the world's 14 peaks above 8,000 meters and attracts climbers from across the globe, although avalanches and rapidly changing weather make expeditions particularly dangerous. https://www.express.co.uk/news/uk/223727.text: Home News UK The camp on Euston Road has been around since 2022 (Image: w8media) More than 40 tents have sprung up on a central London road , with local shopkeepers reporting repeated thefts and anti-social behaviour. Camps on the central reservation of Euston Road are reportedly home to dozens of rough sleepers, many understood to be from Romania and Bulgaria. Local businesses have complained of people allegedly stealing alcohol and solvents, while residents have described intimidation when they attempt to film what is happening. One shopkeeper said: "They steal alcohol and solvents from my shop on a daily basis – I've lost hundreds, if not thousands, in business as a result." He told the Daily Mail: "You call them out, and they get very aggressive; they hate you filming them." The Euston camp is located in Sir Keir Starmer's Holborn and St Pancras constituency . The camp has grown to more than 40 tents since it first appeared in August 2022, despite visits from council homelessness teams and police . Article continues below ADVERTISEMENT A Metropolitan Police spokesperson said officers were aware of the congregation and were working with partners to find a "long-term solution". Article continues below ADVERTISEMENT Camden Council said its priority was to help those sleeping rough "rebuild their lives away from the streets", while also working with partners to ensure the area remained safe and maintained. Speaking to the Daily Mail, Maria, from the Romanian city of Timișoara, claimed she had come to the UK for a "better life" and alleged she had only been in the camp for a month. It was unclear if she was in the UK legally. Asked why she was in the UK, she claimed: "There are no possibilities, no housing in Romania. I am homeless. That's why I am here. "[Camden Council] are wicked, they are not helping me find housing and they are now on holiday. I'm not happy, I cry, I am always very stressed. I don't want to be here." The Daily Express went to the Marble Arch camp with Chris Philp (Image: Jeremy Selwyn) The Daily Express previously exposed an organised Romanian begging gang operating in central London. The investigation found members of the gang had been operating around Marble Arch, with its alleged ringleader Iliuta Gruia previously receiving a restraining order in Romania after threats to kill children. The Express also confronted members of the gang alongside Shadow Home Secretary Chris Philp , who said those found guilty of crimes should be deported. https://telex.hu/belfold/2026/09/14/resz.text: Menü Kereső A melegjogi szervezetek részt vennének az örökbefogadási szabályok újragondolásában Belföld frissítve Kovács Pál Állítsd be a Telexet megbízható forrásnak! Beállítom Több emberi jogi és melegjogi szervezet is részt venne az örökbefogadási szabályok újragondolásában – nyilatkozta több jogvédő az MTI-nek. Magyar Péter épp szombaton, a Pécs Pride napján jelentette be , hogy a kormány kész az azonos nemű párok örökbefogadásával , valamint házasságával kapcsolatos szabályok megváltoztatására. Az Amnesty International Magyarország szerint a miniszterelnök szavai biztató jelek. A szervezeti kommunikációs vezetője, Demeter Áron üdvözölte, hogy „a miniszterelnök is azt az álláspontot képviseli, hogy a szeretet és a szerelem alapjog”. Elmondta, hogy az Orbán-kormány alatt súlyosan korlátozták a szexuális kisebbségek jogait, és ezek a törvények továbbra is érvényben vannak. A szervezet szerint a társadalom többsége támogatja a házasság és az örökbefogadás lehetőségét az azonos nemű párok esetében. A Háttér Társaság képviseletében Dombos Tamás azt mondta, egyre jobban látható, hogy a kormánypárti politikusok a jogegyenlőséget támogatják, és azt ígérik, hogy visszavonják a 2021-ben bevezetett, diszkriminatívnak tartott szabályokat. Szerinte a legfontosabb a közös örökbefogadás lehetővé tétele lenne. A Háttér Társaság rendszeresen ad ki jogegyenlőséget sürgető ajánlásokat, és ha erre lehetőséget kapnak, hivatalosan is átadják ezt a kormánynak. Sürgetőnek tartják a gyülekezési törvényben szereplő, illetve a transznemű emberek névváltoztatását tiltó jogszabályok eltörlését is. Nyilatkozott a Labrisz Leszbikus Egyesület is, amely szintén üdvözli, hogy a kormány szerint ne politikusok, hanem szakemberek döntsenek arról, ki alkalmas egy gyerek örökbefogadására. A szervezet képviselője, Kristófi Mária szerint folyamatosan keresik a kapcsolatot az illetékes minisztériumokkal. A jelenlegi törvények szerint meleg párok a bejegyzett élettársi kapcsolatuk ellenére sem fogadhatnak örökbe közösen gyermeket. Így az azonos nemű párok egyik tagja lehet csak hivatalosan gyám, a másiknak jogilag semmi köze nincs a gyerekhez. Szivárvány Családokért Alapítvány kurátora, Pál Márton szerint az lenne a végső megoldás, ha az azonos nemű párok hivatalosan is összeházasodhatnának. Ő maga is két örökbefogadott gyermeket nevel a férjével, de a jelenlegi törvények miatt csak egyikük lehet gyerekeik hivatalos gyámja. Alapítványukat még nem vonták be a munkába, de Pál Márton szerint felkérés esetén szívesen átadják a tapasztalataikat. Pál Márton és Dombos Tamás hétfőn a Kossuth rádióban is szerepeltek, ahol erről a kérdéskörről beszélgettek – írja a Facebookon a Szivárvány Családokért Alapítvány kurátora. „Lehet, hogy ez csak egy rádióinterjú. Nekünk azonban öt év után óriási szimbolikus jelentősége van. Mert egy olyan ügyben, amelyről hosszú éveken keresztül szinte lehetetlen volt nyilvánosan, őszintén és árnyaltan beszélni, most végre párbeszéd van” – fogalmazott Pál Márton.
